figures.sourceContext: Section 8.1 Proposition 2 and proof: the product topology agrees with the sup-norm metric. Bounded A lies in N'(bar0,p); its closure is the product of compact intervals [-p,p]. A closed bounded subset is therefore compact.
geometry: Four black boundary points, coordinate axes, original coordinate labels and zero label inside the hatched closed sup-norm box.
The source irregular closed A lies strictly inside the open box. Its darker crossing hatches and A knockout are retained; only the consistent subdued orange fill is added.
facts: BoundedBy(A,N'), Subset(A,N'), ClosedIn(A,tau), CompactIn(A,tau), ClosureOf(box,N',tau), ProductOf(box,[-p,p],[-p,p]) and CompactIn(box,tau).
The box has mathematical bounds [-p,-p,p,p]. The diagram uses the source's unequal horizontal and vertical display units; pixel aspect does not change the sup-norm neighborhood.
checks: Positive finite radius validation and immutable product bounds; the factual product, closure and compactness statements are checked.
Native box, irregular set, clipped crossing hatches, four coordinate boundary dots and equation labels render without image elements.
limits: The generic A contour is a style realization of an arbitrary closed bounded subset, not pixel data stored in Substance.
The printed graphic labels Cl N(bar0,p), omitting the prime used in the surrounding proof. That source label is preserved; the bounding neighborhood remains N' semantically.
Smooth vector boundaries and lighter hatches approximate the scan.

figures.sourceContext: Section 8.2 Example 3 and Definition 2 on adjacent printed 169: R^2 is noncompact but locally compact. For arbitrary x and U choose N(x,p) inside U. N(x,p/2) is the interior of the compact closed half-radius disk.
geometry: Original irregular outer U, round N(x,p), central hatched closed half-radius disk, x dot, closure label and short arrow.
The full-radius outline and half-radius hatch use the exact ratio 2:1; no extra outline is added around the hatched disk.
facts: NeighborhoodOf facts, concentric centers and the strict half-radius disk containment chain; InteriorOf, ClosureOf, ClosedIn and CompactIn for the closed disk.
checks: Several boundary samples of the compact disk are strictly inside the outer open disk.
Actual rendered circles retain the radius ratio and common center, and contain the rendered x dot.
limits: The arbitrary U is represented by a smooth style contour. Its generic mathematical identity does not acquire a metric radius.
The source's nearly round handwritten contours become exact circles and smooth cubic boundaries.

figures.sourceContext: Section 8.2 Example 5: assume a compact rational subset A with x in its relative interior. Choose (a,b) intersect Q inside A interior and irrational t in (a,b). The rays U(q) to the side of q away from t form an open cover of A with no finite subcover.
geometry: Original real axis, the two sizes of open parentheses, the interior brace, and direct A interior, a, x, t and b labels.
No extra ray family or shading is introduced into this originally unshaded interval graphic.
facts: AssumedCompactIn(A,tau_Q), not CompactIn; A interior and the interval-relative intersection are named separately.
RationalSubspace Q, induced tau_Q, rational dyadic realization x=5/16, and exact IrrationalPoint expression sqrt2/2 with a separate approximation.
IrrationalInInterval(t,(a,b)), Outside(t,Q), RationalRayCoverAt, OpenCoverOf, HasNoFiniteSubcover and NotLocallyCompact(tau_Q).
checks: The snapshot retains assumed compactness only, with the irrational point outside Q and a genuine rational x inside the relative interval.
For representative finite sets of ray bases, rationalRayGapWitness produces an exact dyadic rational strictly in the remaining gap and in no selected ray.
limits: The chosen x and t are valid representative values; the source does not specify particular rationals or an irrational expression.
The generic assumed interior is not claimed to be the full ambient interval indicated by its schematic outer parentheses.
The finite arithmetic helper validates cover-gap constructions at machine precision; it does not enumerate the infinite rational cover or replace the source argument.

figures.sourceContext: Section 8.2 Proposition 8 and proof: a subspace Y of locally compact Hausdorff X is locally compact exactly when locally closed. Choose relative U'=Y intersect V with compact relative closure, which is also closed in X; this leads to Y open in Cl_X Y and Y=U intersect Cl_X Y.
geometry: Original ambient round X, hatched removed diamond X-Y, smaller V hatch in the opposite direction, their darker overlap, y mark and original Y, X, V and U' labels/leaders.
U' is the part of V lying in Y. Its annotation introduces no extra boundary or extra global U contour.
facts: LocallyCompact(tau_X), T2(tau_X), LocallyCompact(tau_Y), SubspaceTopologyOf and LocallyClosedIn(Y,X,tau_X).
IntersectionOf(U',Y,V), relative OpenIn(U',tau_Y), ambient OpenIn(V,tau_X), compact relative closure with the same entity closed in the ambient topology.
One ClosedSubspace represents Cl_X Y; OpenSubspace Y is OpenIn(Y,tau_ClY), with no OpenIn(Y,tau_X) assertion. Y equals the intersection of an ambient open set U and Cl_X Y.
checks: The snapshot distinguishes relative and ambient topologies while retaining the identity of the closure set.
Actual rendered y lies inside V and above the diamond's highest point, hence outside X-Y. Native reversed hatch clipping and equation labels render successfully.
limits: The generic diamond is a style illustration of the complement; an outlined cartoon does not add a closedness premise for X-Y.
Only the original local sketch is shown; the global open U and closure of Y remain mathematical entities without invented visible contours.
The ambient source contour is reproduced as a nearly circular ellipse.

figures.sourceContext: Section 8.2 Example 6: X={-1} union (0,infinity) is locally compact. Define f(-1)=(0,0) and f(x)=(x,sin(1/x)) for x>0. It is a continuous bijection onto the origin-adjoined graph Y, which is not locally compact. The following definition explains why this map is not open.
geometry: Original left source axis with isolated -1, open positive ray, A/B and x>0 labels, then a mapping arrow to the oscillating target graph.
Target axes and amplitude guides, origin dot, source coordinate labels (0,1),(0,0),(0,-1), and Y annotation.
All curve vertices are genuine positive-x sine samples. The finite high-frequency prefix has a finer stroke to remain legible; there is no filled vertical band or invented vertical segment.
facts: ClopenSingleton A and ClopenHalfLine B are open and closed relative to X, whose union is X; the source's locally-closed construction in R is also retained.
OscillatingSineMap, SineGraphMapOn, SineCurveImageOf, ImageOf, MapsTo(-1,origin), ContinuousMap, OneToOne, Onto, NotOpenMap and FailsLocalCompactnessAt(origin,Y,tau_Y).
Only the origin is adjoined to the positive graph. The marked (0,+/-1) and the fixed-height sequence's ambient limit are explicitly Outside(Y).
checks: Map evaluation rejects 0 and every invalid negative input other than -1.
SineAccumulationTerm yields positive-x graph points tending to (0,height) for nonzero heights. Arbitrarily small tested origin balls contain tails whose ambient limit is outside Y.
Phase steps no larger than pi/12 resolve the canonical native curve; native emitted paths are unfilled, never close, stay strictly right of the origin and within the amplitude guides.

The dense graph's optional ensureOnCanvas flag is false for this fixed, analytically bounded source viewport, avoiding oversized constant path-bbox Wasm compilation. Native render passes with more than 2500 total curve vertices.
limits: The displayed window 0.0015<=x<=0.17 is finite; the semantic graph remains defined for all x>0.
The source is a hand-drawn qualitative sine curve. The analytic rendering has more densely resolved oscillations near zero; stroke refinement controls aliasing but pixel identity is not claimed.
The ordinary curve still uses true affine coordinate units, without distorting x, joining the graph to the origin, or adding the vertical accumulation segment.
The numerical sequence tests check constructive witnesses at sampled radii; the complete universal local-compactness argument remains in the supplied book prose.
